articles.title: First launch
articles.summary: Start manually or configure optional AI providers.
steps: Choose New Project to see every supported starting path.
Manual editing and Manual Guided work without an AI provider.
Open Settings only if you want to configure Text, Vision or Image generation.
Use Quick Actions from the sidebar or Ctrl+K to find commands by name.
notes: Character Card Forge does not contact an AI provider until you explicitly request an AI action.

articles.title: Set up AI providers
articles.summary: Configure Text, Vision and Image roles independently.
steps: Open Settings and configure a Primary Text profile for character writing.
Assign Fast Text or Deep Review only when you want a different profile for those tasks; Use Primary is the default.
Configure Vision separately for image analysis and Image Generation separately for artwork.
Use each profile's connection or discovery controls before starting important work.
notes: Fallback is optional and should use a distinct profile. It handles bounded technical failures, not refusals or invalid content.
API keys stay in local app settings and are omitted from support reports and exported cards.

articles.title: Create your first character
articles.summary: Choose a creation route, review the draft and export deliberately.
steps: Choose New Project and select Blank Workspace, Manual Guided, Idea Generator, Character Collaborator, Idea Notebook or Template Start.
Select the starting template and confirm Create Project.
For AI routes, review proposed content before accepting it into the editable Workspace.
Check Description, Personality, Scenario and First Message, then save the project.
Add or generate artwork before PNG export when you want a visual card.
notes: Filling in Generation Concept alone does not create the finished character fields. Run Generate Character and review the result first.

articles.title: Import an existing character
articles.summary: Preview supported card or project files before copying, merging or replacing.
steps: Choose New Project, select Import Card or Project and confirm.
Select a supported Character Card PNG/APNG/JSON or Character Card Forge project package.
Review the detected format, portrait, validation, duplicate evidence and loss mapping.
Choose Copy, Merge or Replace only after the preview matches your intent.
notes: Merge and Replace retain recovery information where the workflow supports it; they are never automatic.

articles.title: Edit, inspect and improve a character
articles.summary: Use the Workspace, Card Inspector, AI Review and Revision History safely.
steps: Edit canonical fields directly in the Workspace and save meaningful progress.
Use Card Inspector for deterministic health checks, token estimates and export-facing metadata.
Run AI Review only when wanted; inspect every finding and proposed replacement.
Approve fields selectively. Rejected changes remain rejected and the accepted batch creates a recovery checkpoint.
Use Revision History to compare, restore, fork or selectively recover earlier values.
notes: AI scores are advisory, not objective measures of character quality.

articles.title: Find and organise characters
articles.summary: Search, filter, group and resize the Character Library.
steps: Open Character Library and search across projects, characters, card text and metadata.
Use workflow, review, token, Front Porch, privacy and deployment filters to narrow results.
Assign series, tags, folders and collections from Project Tools or batch actions.
Use Panels to collapse Filters, Project Tools or Details, and adjust card density for the available space.
Archive recoverably instead of deleting work you may need later.
notes: Portable/shared-folder libraries use a documented single-writer model; they are not automatic cloud sync.

articles.title: Create and manage artwork
articles.summary: Compose creative intent separately from provider execution settings.
steps: Open Image Studio and choose the active project and character.
Write or generate a character-aware prompt, then apply creative style controls or a reusable style preset.
Choose the Image profile, model or workflow and only the operations that its discovered capabilities support.
Run generation explicitly, compare results and accept the chosen image into managed project assets.
Use Avatar Gallery or Generate Expression Set for Front Porch alternate looks and expressions.
notes: Browsing results, editing presets and composing prompts do not call an Image provider.
Reference, Image-to-Image and Inpainting inputs are explicit and never inferred from unrelated Vision attachments.

articles.title: Export a character
articles.summary: Preview the target format and artwork before writing a card.
steps: Open Export or Install from a saved Workspace project.
Choose the target export profile and inspect the exact mapped, preserved, transformed and omitted fields.
Resolve the unfinished-character safety check if all core roleplay fields are empty.
Choose artwork for PNG output, or explicitly confirm a definition-only export when supported.
Select a destination and complete the local export.
notes: Character Card Forge warns about missing artwork because a successful JSON definition can otherwise look like a failed PNG export.

articles.title: Connect and install to Front Porch
articles.summary: Use supported APIs and portable formats without direct database writes.
steps: Open Export or Install and configure the Front Porch address for the current session.
Run Connection Diagnostics to verify reachability, authentication and supported endpoints.
Sign in when required; passwords, two-factor codes and cookies are not persisted.
Preview collisions and remote differences before Create Copy, Update or Replace actions.
Use supported APIs or portable files for characters, groups, worlds, galleries and chats.
notes: Character Card Forge never reads or writes the Front Porch SQLite database.
Optional Front Porch character-life fields do not enter ordinary cards unless the target format carries that extension.

articles.title: Back up and recover work
articles.summary: Protect projects, revisions and portable libraries before risky changes.
steps: Keep backups of the active Character Card Forge library or portable library folder while the app is closed.
Use Revision History checkpoints for field-level comparison, selective recovery, restore or fork.
Use Archive for recoverable Library removal and project packages for portable project copies.
If a portable share is unavailable, reconnect it and reopen the project from that library; do not create a substitute path.
Resolve external-change conflicts by reviewing both copies instead of overwriting blindly.
notes: Portable/shared folders are single-writer. Close the project on one computer before editing it on another.

articles.title: Troubleshoot a problem
articles.summary: Capture the narrowest useful evidence without exposing private content.
steps: Repeat the smallest action that shows the problem and record what you expected and what happened.
For generation failures, open that job's Generation Diagnostics and review the credential-redacted request summary.
For Front Porch problems, run Connection Diagnostics and note which supported capability failed.
Open Support & Diagnostics for the app/environment summary; model identifiers remain optional.
Create a bug report with reproducible steps, the app version and only the diagnostic files you reviewed.
notes: Never post API keys, passwords, cookies, private character text or private chat transcripts in a public issue.

articles.title: Diagnostics and privacy
articles.summary: Understand what the general support report includes and excludes.
steps: Open Support & Diagnostics and read the complete report preview.
Leave model identifiers disabled unless the provider/model is relevant to the problem.
Copy or export the report only after reviewing it.
Use Open Bug Report only when ready; the app never submits the report automatically.
notes: The general report always omits character/project content, prompts, conversations, credentials, sessions, endpoint addresses, custom profile names and file paths.

articles.title: Install Character Card Forge
articles.summary: Choose the correct package, extract it and keep your projects separate from the application folder.
steps: Download the package for your platform from the official GitHub Release.
Verify the published checksum when you need independent package-integrity confirmation.
Extract the complete archive to a writable application folder and launch Character Card Forge.
On unsigned macOS builds, review the documented platform warning before choosing whether to open the app.
notes: Updates never silently replace a running installation. Project libraries remain separate from application files.

articles.title: Manual editing and Manual Guided
articles.summary: Create complete cards without an AI provider or use a step-by-step manual flow.
steps: Choose New Project, then select Blank Workspace for direct editing or Manual Guided for a stepped workflow.
Choose a template and confirm Create Project.
Fill the canonical character fields and optional sections at your own pace.
Save the project, inspect it and export only when the preview matches your intent.
notes: Manual authoring does not require provider configuration or network access.

articles.title: Use Character Builder
articles.summary: Assemble appearance, personality and scene direction from editable structured choices.
steps: Open the Builder from a character project and choose the section you want to develop.
Select, edit or add options instead of accepting a preset as fixed content.
Review the assembled result before applying it to canonical character fields.
Use normal Workspace editing for any final prose or continuity adjustments.
notes: Builder presets are starting structures and never prevent manual changes.

articles.title: Idea Generator and Idea Notebook
articles.summary: Generate several concepts, keep useful ideas and deliberately choose what becomes a project.
steps: Choose Idea Generator when you want several candidate concepts from explicit options.
Choose Quick, Standard, Detailed or Extended for a preset depth, or Custom to enter an approximate character target for each idea's concept.
Set the total Ideas up to 50, then choose 1–12 Ideas per provider request; use 1 for smaller models and review the disclosed request count before generating.
Review the complete results and save promising ideas to Idea Notebook; choose New Notebook beside the destination when the batch needs its own notebook.
Choose Import Idea Pack to validate and preview a .ccfideas.json file; resolve stable-ID conflicts before confirming the atomic import.
Use notebook-name search, notebook and idea sorting, tags, idea text search and archive visibility to manage large collections.
In All Ideas, use the notebook label beneath each title to understand cross-notebook search and sorting results.
Edit saved ideas or combine your own notes before starting a character.
Choose Export Idea Pack to share selected entries, a Bible, a Series or the complete notebook while retaining structured rules and custom sections.
Create a project only from the idea you intentionally choose.
notes: Idea generation preserves user agency and does not make brainstorming canonical automatically.
The default remains up to 12 ideas per request, so the ordinary six-idea workflow still makes one provider call. Smaller request sizes increase the number of calls and may increase usage.
Successful request batches are combined in order; if one request fails, completed ideas remain available instead of being discarded.
A Custom character target is a model-guided request, not a guarantee. The completion status reports actual minimum, maximum and average concept lengths.
Large Custom requests are capped by the configured Text model/profile maximum output; an off-target but otherwise valid idea remains reviewable.
Newer unsupported Idea Pack schemas may be previewed but are not imported silently.

articles.title: Develop a character with Character Collaborator
articles.summary: Brainstorm conversationally, manage evidence and create a reviewed Blueprint handoff.
steps: Start Character Collaborator from New Project or send one explicit existing character for refinement.
Add reference sources and assign evidence roles when several sources have different authority.
Develop the character until the conversation contains the detail you want preserved.
Create the Generation Blueprint, review its supplementary greetings and Lorebook, then choose the destination draft.
Use rewind when you need to remove later conversation turns without deleting independent references.
notes: Conversation remains non-canonical until you explicitly create or apply a draft.

articles.title: Templates and generation modes
articles.summary: Choose field structure and generation depth without mixing templates with character content.
steps: Choose a template when creating the project; confirm it before the project is created.
Use the generation mode that matches the desired depth and available model limits.
Review generated sections before applying them, especially after changing models or providers.
Keep reusable structural defaults in templates and character-specific facts in the project.
notes: A larger generation mode never bypasses the configured model output ceiling.

articles.title: Workspace and task layouts
articles.summary: Keep the editor focused by opening the controls needed for the current task.
steps: Use the Editing layout for normal character fields.
Switch to Review, Lorebook, Front Porch Deployment or Group Card when that is the active task.
Use the field navigation shortcuts for long templates.
Save before closing when the Workspace reports unsaved changes.

articles.title: Alternative Greetings and Scenario Presets
articles.summary: Manage alternate openings and reusable setups without duplicating the full character.
steps: Open the Alternative Greetings manager to add, edit, categorize, weight or favourite openings.
Create Scenario Presets for alternate setups, active cast, tags and shared-world references.
Preview the selected scenario and opening together before export or testing.
Materialise one explicit scenario when the target format cannot carry multiple setups.
notes: The standard Character Card alternative-greetings array remains synchronized.

articles.title: Lorebooks and Relationships
articles.summary: Author triggerable context and explicit character links without creating a second source of truth.
steps: Open Lorebook Manager and choose Project or Character scope.
Give every entry a meaningful editable name, primary keys and focused lore content.
Use Trigger Preview with sample scene text to check which entries activate.
Create Relationships or Linked Variants only when the connection is intentional and inspectable.
notes: Content and trigger warnings belong in author notes, not in the entry name.

articles.title: Inspect card health and metadata
articles.summary: Run deterministic checks, inspect token size and repair structural problems before export.
steps: Open Card Inspector from the saved character project.
Review deterministic health findings and whole-card or section token estimates.
Inspect compiled-prompt and technical views with their stated limitations.
Use validated Raw JSON or repair actions only when you understand the affected structure.
notes: Card Inspector does not call an AI model and its compiled prompt is explicitly approximate.

articles.title: Run AI Review safely
articles.summary: Treat ratings as advisory and approve proposed field changes individually.
steps: Save the current character, then explicitly run AI Review.
Read the full findings report and inspect each proposed before-and-after field value.
Keep every proposal rejected until you deliberately approve it.
Apply the selected batch only after the source hash is still current.
notes: The score uses a visible rubric and is not an objective measure of character quality.

articles.title: Compare and recover revisions
articles.summary: Use immutable checkpoints to inspect, restore, fork or selectively recover earlier character values.
steps: Open Revision History and select two meaningful checkpoints to compare.
Inspect complete field values instead of relying only on shortened summaries.
Apply selected earlier fields, create a fork or restore non-destructively.
Export an earlier revision as ordinary Character Card V2 JSON when needed.
notes: Large assets remain managed references and private revision lineage stays out of ordinary card exports.

articles.title: Create Compact or Lite derivatives
articles.summary: Produce a smaller independent character while protecting the full source card.
steps: Choose the target token budget, compression intent and fields that must be preserved.
Review every proposed replacement and edit or reject individual changes.
Confirm only while the source content hash is still current.
Save the new independent character and retain its private source lineage.
notes: Compact/Lite never overwrites the source character or reuses its Front Porch identity.

articles.title: Search, filters and saved views
articles.summary: Combine full-library search with explainable filters and reusable views.
steps: Search by project, character, series, card text, tags, creators or import metadata.
Add workflow, review, token, Front Porch, privacy or deployment filters.
Save a named view when the combination supports a repeated task.
Use a Smart Collection only when membership should follow saved criteria.

articles.title: Collections, tags and workflow states
articles.summary: Organise projects without changing their exported character definitions.
steps: Select one or more projects in Character Library.
Assign series, folders, collections and concise tags from Project Tools or batch actions.
Use workflow states such as Draft or Stable to reflect authoring status.
Review each batch outcome instead of assuming every project changed.
notes: Private Library organisation is separate from ordinary Character Card exports.

articles.title: Handle duplicates and archived projects
articles.summary: Review duplicate evidence and keep removed projects recoverable.
steps: Open duplicate review and compare exact IDs, hashes or normalized-text evidence.
Choose Merge, Replace, Keep Both or Ignore only after inspecting both projects.
Use Archive for recoverable removal from normal Library views.
Enable Show archived when you need to inspect or restore archived work.
notes: Duplicate detection and archive actions never run automatically.

articles.title: Adult and private presentation controls
articles.summary: Mark sensitive projects and choose how artwork appears locally.
steps: Set Adult or Private markers in project workflow metadata when appropriate.
Choose Show, Blur Artwork or Hide as the local presentation policy.
Use Library sensitivity filters to control what is visible during browsing.
Explicitly reveal hidden content only when the current setting allows it.
notes: Presentation controls reduce accidental display; they are not encryption or access control.

articles.title: Portable, shared-folder and NAS libraries
articles.summary: Use a shared location with explicit single-writer and recovery boundaries.
steps: Open Settings → Library Storage and inspect the current library before changing it.
Initialize or select the intended portable folder explicitly.
Close the project on one computer before editing it from another.
If the share disappears or changes externally, reconnect and review the conflict instead of substituting another path.
notes: Shared-folder mode is not concurrent multi-user editing or automatic cloud synchronization.

articles.title: Library panels, auto-hide and card density
articles.summary: Recover card space while keeping every Library panel easy to restore.
steps: Use the edge arrows to collapse or reveal Library Filters and Project Details.
Open Panels for Show all panels or Focus card area presets.
Enable side-panel auto-hide only when you want panels to collapse after returning to the card area.
Adjust card density; smaller cards progressively hide metadata and overlay the name on artwork.

articles.title: Create a multi-character project
articles.summary: Build a cast from new members, Library copies or both.
steps: Choose New Multi-Character / Group Project from the supported creation surface.
Add a new member or copy an existing Library character into the project.
Edit each member as an independent character while sharing explicit project context.
Use Card Workflow Studio when you want a combined runtime or Front Porch group card.
notes: Adding an existing Library character creates an independent project member rather than silently editing the source.

articles.title: Group cards and Split Character Sets
articles.summary: Choose between one ensemble artifact and several independently generated cards.
steps: Use a group card when the target runtime should coordinate several characters in one artifact.
Use Split Character Set when each planned member needs an independent complete card.
Review group prompts, opening state and member voices before materialising the combined artifact.
For split generation, retain successful members and retry only failed or pending members.
notes: Group materialisation never silently merges or overwrites the independent source characters.

articles.title: Persistent rosters, active cast and shared worlds
articles.summary: Keep project membership separate from who appears in a particular opening or scenario.
steps: Maintain the complete persistent roster in the multi-character project.
Select only the active or present cast for a scenario when the target supports that distinction.
Reference shared world records instead of copying their lore into every character.
Inspect dependencies before removing referenced characters, worlds, images or workflows.

articles.title: Image styles and Generation Profiles
articles.summary: Separate reusable creative direction from provider and workflow execution settings.
steps: Choose or edit a Global, Project Visual Identity or Character Default style preset.
Compose the editable Image Prompt from structured creative controls when ready.
Choose a Generation Profile for provider, model, checkpoint or ComfyUI workflow execution.
Review discovered capabilities and explicit overrides before generating.
notes: Style presets never store credentials, model choices, sampler settings, seeds or ComfyUI workflows.

articles.title: Image-to-Image, references and Inpainting
articles.summary: Attach explicit image inputs only to operations the selected profile can perform.
steps: Choose Image-to-Image, Reference or Inpainting as the explicit operation.
Select the managed source image and a mask where Inpainting requires one.
Set operation-specific strength or influence without changing unrelated Vision attachments.
Generate only after the active profile reports executable support for that operation.
notes: Unknown capability metadata is not treated as proven support, and image inputs are never inferred.

articles.title: Portraits, Avatar Gallery and Expression Sets
articles.summary: Manage a canonical portrait, alternate looks and reviewable expression batches.
steps: Accept or import images into the managed Avatar Gallery.
Choose the canonical favourite independently from the Character Card portrait.
Generate an Expression Set by selecting exact labels and one explicit visual baseline.
Review, retry or replace each expression independently before ZIP export or Front Porch installation.
notes: Expression generation creates separate provider jobs and never installs results automatically.

articles.title: Export profiles and target previews
articles.summary: Inspect how each target maps, transforms, preserves or omits project data.
steps: Choose the Character Card V2, Front Porch, SillyTavern or another available export profile.
Review the exact before-export mapping and preservation report.
Resolve unsupported or omitted fields before writing the file.
Export JSON or image-embedded card data only after confirming the final target preview.
notes: Unknown imported fields remain preserved where the adapter contract supports lossless round trips.

articles.title: Export and import project packages
articles.summary: Move complete Character Card Forge projects with their managed assets and private authoring data.
steps: Save the project and open Import / Export.
Export a project package when you need more than an ordinary runtime character card.
Keep the complete package archive intact while transferring it.
On import, review validation, duplicate evidence and the proposed Copy, Merge or Replace action.
notes: Project packages can contain private authoring state that ordinary Character Card exports intentionally omit.

articles.title: Add PDF and URL reference sources
articles.summary: Preview bounded local extraction or HTTPS downloads before they enter AI context.
steps: Add a PDF or use Add from URL for a supported bounded HTTPS source.
Review detected type, extracted text, image or readable document preview.
Explicitly choose whether accepted text becomes AI-facing context.
Use Refresh Remote only when you want a new preview; references never refresh in the background.
notes: Remote text is untrusted data. Scanned PDFs remain stored without silently invoking OCR.

articles.title: Install, update and sync Front Porch characters
articles.summary: Compare local and remote state before using supported authenticated APIs.
steps: Run Connection Diagnostics and authenticate for the current session.
Review Not Installed, Installed, Modified Locally, Changed in Front Porch or Diverged state.
Compare local and remote data before Update, Reinstall or Import Front Porch Changes.
Use the deployment queue for explicit sequential work and inspect every result.
notes: CCF uses supported APIs and never falls back to direct database access.

articles.title: Author optional Front Porch character-life fields
articles.summary: Set character-life, Needs, relationship and opening-state extensions manually or with reviewed AI suggestions.
steps: Open the Front Porch — Optional Workspace tab.
Enter fields manually or use AI Suggest for the selected field or enabled group.
Review every proposal before including it in the project.
Leave all fields empty when the character should emit no Front Porch extension.
notes: Relationship history is not invented for the user, and intimate preferences require adult-content opt-in.

articles.title: Exchange Front Porch group cards and worlds
articles.summary: Use portable group PNG and world packages while preserving unknown future data.
steps: Build and validate the group workflow or world record before export.
Review member cards, shared opening, world lore and private-context warnings.
Export the supported portable group PNG or .fpworld package.
Use direct installation only when Front Porch proves the required supported endpoint.
notes: Stoop publishing and unsupported group endpoints remain disabled; unknown imported fields are preserved.

articles.title: Test Chat and chat exchange
articles.summary: Test a saved character through Front Porch and transfer chat history separately from authored card data.
steps: Create or choose an explicit Local Test Profile without changing the character definition.
Start Test Chat only after Front Porch proves the required chat capabilities.
Send, stream, cancel and refresh history through the supported API.
Import or export .fpchat or compatible JSON/JSONL with validation and provenance.
notes: Chat history and evolving simulation state remain separate from authored card data.

articles.title: Primary, Fast, Deep Review and Fallback Text routes
articles.summary: Assign task-specific Text profiles while retaining one clear default.
steps: Configure Primary Text as the default character-writing route.
Assign Fast / Suggestion Text or Deep Review Text only when those tasks need another profile.
Enable Fallback only with a distinct profile and review the bounded failure types it can handle.
Inspect completed job metadata to see the profile and model that actually produced the result.
notes: Fallback never switches models for refusals, invalid output, parsing errors or validation failures.

articles.title: Configure Vision and Image profiles
articles.summary: Keep image analysis and artwork generation independent from Text generation.
steps: Configure Vision for explicit image analysis and choose its independent model limits.
Configure Image Generation profiles for cloud, local Forge/A1111 or ComfyUI workflows.
Run discovery or connection tests before important work.
Review capability provenance and explicit overrides rather than assuming OpenAI-compatible servers support identical routes.

articles.title: Manage storage and application updates
articles.summary: Choose Library storage deliberately and keep update installation explicit.
steps: Use Settings → Library Storage to inspect or select the active project library.
Use cache controls only for disposable local thumbnails; original artwork is never a cache target.
Choose Check for Updates manually or keep the disclosed daily check enabled.
Review release notes and download the exact platform package; installation remains manual.
notes: Update checks send no provider credentials or project data and never replace a running executable.

articles.title: Diagnostics and expert functions
articles.summary: Use technical views for evidence and repair without bypassing normal validation boundaries.
steps: Open the narrow diagnostic surface for the failed provider job, import or Front Porch action.
Review the complete credential-redacted preview before copying or exporting it.
Use expert Raw JSON only through its validator and keep a revision or project backup.
Return to the normal editor to confirm the repaired data still behaves as expected.
notes: Expert controls do not weaken credential, path, validation or confirmation safeguards.

articles.title: Known limitations and reporting a bug
articles.summary: Check the current support boundary and send a reproducible privacy-reviewed report.
steps: Check the current release notes and Help Center for a stated limitation or supported configuration.
Reproduce the problem with the smallest safe sequence and record expected versus actual behavior.
Generate and review the privacy-safe support report and any relevant per-job diagnostic.
Open the GitHub bug report and attach only the evidence you intentionally reviewed.
notes: Current macOS packages are unsigned; third-party providers and shared/NAS storage still require real-world compatibility evidence.
